haiku-low.q1: Keys load before the HTTP listener starts. /healthz returns 200 only after the startup load of all three secrets succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs the error without values and exits non-zero. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: A background task re-reads each secret every 300 seconds and swaps in a changed, non-empty value, logging the new version id. On failure it keeps the last good value and logs a WARN.
haiku-low.q4: Values live only in memory, in the secret cache (value and version_id per key). They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, in logs, or in exception messages.
haiku-low.q5: Production pods read prod values through workload identity. Only the security on-call role writes them. Engineers have no read access to prod.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history and container images, so deleting them is not enough. Revoking them at each provider makes the old values harmless.
haiku-low.q7: Clients stop copying the key in their constructors. Each request reads the current value from the cache and builds the Authorization header then.
haiku-low.q8: Each instance exposes its loaded version_id per secret on an internal endpoint or metric. Step 7 confirms all pods report the new version_id before any revocation.
haiku-low.q9: Access is set before step 3. Then: create provider keys (step 2), copy values to the store (step 3), merge the code and config removal (step 4), deploy (step 6), revoke old keys last (step 9).
haiku-low.q10: make run uses the same loader against orders-api/dev/*, through the developer's own store session, which reads dev only. Sandbox keys are used. No .env file holds keys.
haiku-low.q11: The whole load fails, because any read failure or empty value fails it. The app retries 3 times, then exits non-zero. It does not start with only two keys.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. No rotation cadence is chosen; security has not decided whether scheduled rotation is required (open question 1).

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded before the HTTP listener starts; /healthz (readiness) returns 200 only after the startup load of all three succeeds.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 attempt + 3 retries, 2s apart, ~6s), then logs the error without values and exits non-zero. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving with their old in-memory keys, so live traffic is unaffected (though a restart during an outage reduces capacity).
sonnet.q3: A background task every 300 seconds reads each secret's current version; if the version id changed and value is non-empty, it swaps the cache entry and logs the new version id. On any failure it keeps the last good entry and logs a WARN (secret name, kept version id, error class); readiness stays 200.
sonnet.q4: In the in-memory secret cache (value and version_id per key, lock-guarded, swapped atomically). They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs (Authorization header redacted in debug logs, exception messages and reprs).
sonnet.q5: Read: only the orders-api-prod pods (read on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call role. Engineers have no read on prod.
sonnet.q6: Old values remain in git history (and may stay in central logs up to 30 days) and in existing images. What makes them harmless is that the old keys are revoked at the providers (after rotation); git history is not rewritten.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key in constructors; on each request they read the current value from the secret cache and build the Authorization header then.
sonnet.q8: Via the confirmation signal: each instance exposes loaded version_id per secret on an internal endpoint or metric (never values). Step 7 checks no pod runs a pre-migration image, every pod reports the new version_id for all three secrets, and error rates/401-403 are at baseline.
sonnet.q9: Step 1 verify overlapping keys; 2 create new keys at providers (rotation); 3 write keys to the store (store access/IAM is set up and simulated before step 3); 4 merge code that reads from the store and removes api_key from config (same change); then deploy, confirm, grace period, and revoke old keys. Access setup is stated only as being verified before step 3; its exact placement relative to steps 1-2 is not stated.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store path orders-api/dev/* (sandbox provider keys), loaded by the same loader via make run, using the developer's own store session/identity, which reads dev only. No .env file with keys is written.
sonnet.q11: If any read fails or returns an empty value, the whole load fails; it retries (up to 3 retries, 2s apart), and if all attempts fail it logs the error without values and exits non-zero. (A missing secret is not explicitly described, but it would be a failed read.)
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Rotation cadence is an open question; no schedule is chosen.
